battle.name: 第一次塞米諾爾戰爭
battle.theater: 佛羅里達西北阿帕拉契科河下游
battle.brief: 一八一七年十二月，傑克遜率縱隊越過聖瑪麗河進入西班牙佛羅里達，追討克里克戰爭的逃亡者；次年三月主力沿阿帕拉契科河推進，焚燒黑堡與密卡蘇基村社，迫使塞米諾爾人退入沼澤。卡面的長槍是西班牙方陣時代的舊物，一八一七年只剩軍械庫裡的殘件與對手的長矛，戰線上列陣的已是刺刀滑膛槍與野戰砲。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 交戰的兩方分處兩個制度完全不同的世界。美國一方以南方部為骨架：一八一七年十二月二十六日，戰爭部長約翰·卡爾霍恩下令讓安德魯·傑克遜親自指揮對佛羅里達的行動；到一八一八年三月在喬治亞州弗林特河畔的斯科特堡集合時，隊伍包括八百名美軍正規步兵、一千名田納西志願兵、一千名喬治亞民兵，以及約一千四百名由克里克族准將威廉·麥金托什率領的下克里克盟友，另有黑人士兵擔任廚役、搬運手與嚮導。西班牙在法律上仍是佛羅里達的宗主：東、西佛羅里達總督府分設於聖奧古斯丁與彭薩科拉，要塞群包括聖馬爾科斯、彭薩科拉與巴蘭卡斯堡，但守軍單薄、命令難以到達，一八一八年五月彭薩科拉城守備隊只有一百七十五人，聖馬克斯也只剩殘缺的分遣隊，而西班牙本土正處自由主義時期，王室自顧不暇。塞米諾爾一方並非國家，而是一個聯盟：塞米諾爾、密卡蘇基與克里克村社，同黑堡的黑人社群、克里克戰爭與莫爾特里堡逃出的追奴者結在一起，沒有常備軍，靠村社民兵與戰鬥小隊作戰，首領如彼得·麥昆、比莉·鮑萊茲、霍默·普拉默、尼馬特拉等。英國不在佛州駐軍，卻以巴哈馬為基地向塞米諾爾人供應火器，陸戰隊中尉理查德·卡特在黑堡率領英軍，僑居巴哈馬的蘇格蘭商人亞歷山大·喬治·阿布思諾特在佛州做貿易並替他們傳遞文書。
countriesEn: The two sides belonged to two entirely different worlds. On the American side stood the regular army of the United States organised as the Department of the South: on 26 December 1817 the Secretary of War, John C. Calhoun, ordered Andrew Jackson to take personal command of the operation against Florida, and when the force assembled at Fort Scott on the Flint River in Georgia in March 1818 it comprised eight hundred regular infantry, a thousand Tennessee volunteers, a thousand Georgia militia and some fourteen hundred Lower Creek allies under the Creek-born Brigadier General William McIntosh, together with black soldiers serving as cooks, drivers and guides. Spain was the legal sovereign of Florida: the East and West Florida governments sat at St. Augustine and Pensacola, and the chain of forts included San Marcos de Apalache, Pensacola and Fort Barrancas, but the garrisons were thin and the orders travelled badly; in May 1818 the garrison of the city of Pensacola numbered only one hundred and seventy-five men, while St. Marks was held by a detachment reduced to a handful, and Spain at the time was in the Liberal Experiment, with the crown unable to attend to anything beyond the peninsula itself. The Seminole side was not a state but a confederacy: Seminole, Mikasuki and Creek villages joined with the black community of Negro Fort, with the runaways of the Creek War and of Fort Moultrie, and it had no standing army, fighting through village militias and war bands under leaders such as Peter McQueen, Billy Bowlegs, Homer Plummer and Neamathla. Britain kept no troops in Florida but supplied the Seminoles with firearms from the Bahamas, a British marine officer, Lieutenant Richard Carter, led the British at Negro Fort, and a Scottish trader resident in the Bahamas, Alexander George Arbuthnot, traded in Florida and carried correspondence for the Indians.
people: 安德魯·傑克遜是這場戰爭的推手與象徵。他自一八一五年新奧良之戰後被調回國內，一八一七年出任南方部司令，駐地就在弗林特河畔的斯科特堡；一八一七年十二月二十六日，卡爾霍恩的越境命令送到他手上，他於次年三月十五日率主力沿阿帕拉契科河越境，一路焚燒密卡蘇基與紅棍村社，四月七日佔領聖馬克斯，五月二十八日迫使彭薩科拉的巴蘭卡斯堡投降，九月回到斯科特堡宣布戰事結束。威廉·溫菲爾德·斯科特中校是最重要的縱隊指揮官，他率一八一八年一月的深入縱隊穿越威拉庫奇河沼澤，二月十九至二十日在奧基喬比湖東岸的林莽交火，以六磅砲清出林緣射擊線，付出全戰役最重的美軍傷亡。威廉·麥金托什是克里克出身的准將，率下克里克與志願兵，於一八一八年四月十二日在埃康菲納河攻擊彼得·麥昆率領的紅棍聚落，麥昆陣亡。約翰·麥金托什是克里克戰爭的老將，以民兵首領身分參與福爾敦與黑哈奇等村社的攻擊，並於一八一七年十一月三十日在阿帕拉契科河伏擊了斯科特中尉的補給船，即所謂的斯科特慘案，華盛頓正是為此改變態度。埃德蒙·彭德爾頓·蓋恩斯中將駐守斯科特堡，主持福爾敦之役與後勤；理查德·阿布克利中校是堡內駐軍指揮官，管的是船隊與給養。西班牙方面，聖馬克斯守將弗朗西斯科·卡索·路恩戈在一八一八年四月六日收到傑克遜的書信，第二天要塞便被美軍佔領；被美軍視為戰爭煽動者的英籍人士中，商人亞歷山大·喬治·阿布思諾特被絞死，羅伯特·阿姆布里斯特於四月二十九日被行刑隊處決。塞米諾爾一方沒有將軍，首領靠名望與影響力取勝：彼得·麥昆是規模最大的戰士首領之一，在埃康菲納河陣亡；比莉·鮑萊茲坐鎮鮑萊茲村，黑人首領尼羅重建了黑堡的武裝；霍默·普拉默與尼馬特拉先後代表村社與美軍交涉；喬西亞斯·弗朗西斯原是克里克語通譯，後成為塞米諾爾陣營中最重要的說客，他與霍馬特萊米科在一艘掛美國旗的船附近被誘捕，未經審判即在聖馬克斯被絞殺。
peopleEn: Andrew Jackson was the driving force and the symbol of the war. After the Battle of New Orleans in 1815 he was recalled home, and in 1817 he took command of the Department of the South with his headquarters at Fort Scott on the Flint River; the order from Calhoun to cross the border reached him on 26 December 1817, and on 15 March of the following year he led the main body across the Apalachicola, burning the Mikasuki and Red Stick villages as he went, taking St. Marks on 7 April, forcing the surrender of Fort Barrancas at Pensacola on 28 May, and returning to Fort Scott in September to declare the war over. Lieutenant Colonel Winfield Scott was the most important column commander: his deep column of January 1818 crossed the Withlacoochee swamp, and on 19 and 20 February he fought in the hammock on the east shore of Lake Okeechobee, clearing the firing line with his six-pounders at the cost of the heaviest American losses of the campaign. William McIntosh, a Creek and brigadier general, led the Lower Creeks and the volunteers, and on 12 April 1818 struck Peter McQueen's Red Stick settlement on the Econfina River, where McQueen was killed. John McIntosh was a veteran of the Creek War who led militia raids on villages such as Fowltown and Black Hachee, and on 30 November 1817 he ambushed Lieutenant Richard Scott's supply boat on the Apalachicola in the so-called Scott massacre, and it was that affair which changed Washington's mind. Edmund Pendleton Gaines held Fort Scott, directed the attack on Fowltown and ran the logistics; Richard Arbuckle, commanding at the fort, looked after the boats and the supply trains. On the Spanish side, the commandant of St. Marks, Francisco Caso y Luengo, received Jackson's letter on 6 April 1818, and the next day the fort was occupied by American troops. Of the British subjects the Americans held to be the instigators, the trader Alexander George Arbuthnot was hanged, and Robert Ambrister was shot by a firing squad on 29 April. The Seminoles had no generals; their leaders ruled by standing and influence. Peter McQueen was among the largest of the war chiefs and fell at the Econfina; Billy Bowlegs held Bowlegs Town; the black chief Nero rebuilt the armed community of Negro Fort; Homer Plummer and Neamathla spoke for the villages in turn; and Josiah Francis, once an interpreter in Creek, became the most important spokesman of the Seminole cause before he and Homathlemico were lured aboard a vessel flying the United States flag and hanged at St. Marks without trial.
kits: 長槍在這場戰爭裡的位置，是一件早已退場、卻仍留有餘溫的兵器。卡面上那支一六〇〇年的長槍代表的是西班牙大方陣時代的槍盾陣：長矛手站在前排，用矛幹與矛叢擋住對面的衝撞與火槍，後排的火槍手趁裝填的間隙齊射，射完退回矛後再裝；方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面，正是這個道理。三十年之後，槍盾陣在歐洲已被刺刀與燧發槍全面取代，一八一七年的佛羅里達前線，美軍線列步兵裝的是一八一二式與一八一四年式燧發滑膛槍配刺刀，戰場上再也沒有成排的長槍。但退場不等於消失。其一，西班牙殖民軍在佛州各要塞的軍械庫裡仍存有十六、十七世紀方陣時代留下的長槍與舊式長矛，一八一八年聖馬克斯與彭薩科拉易手時，這些存械隨之流入美軍手中，只是它們早已不在任何戰鬥序列裡，具體件數史無明文，可確認者僅止於此。其二，真正還握著長柄刺器的，是塞米諾爾與克里克戰士，以及編入美軍的克里克與切羅基輔助部隊：他們攜帶長柄矛、標槍與弓箭，在近身衝擊與追擊時使用，並與火槍配合，這正是卡面那句「密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了」的意思——同一件兵器在兩個時代的兩種用法。其三，槍盾陣的邏輯在一八一八年的攻堅中被火炮徹底取代：黑堡的木柵與土壘取代了矛牆，防御方以九門砲封住阿帕拉契科河口，進攻方用六磅野戰砲與十二磅榴砲在數百碼外轟擊；一八一六年摧毀黑堡的更是一發灼熱彈打進火藥庫。其他裝備方面，美軍有線列滑膛槍配刺刀、六磅砲與十二磅榴砲、騎兵卡賓槍與馬刀，後勤靠騾馬、軍用車、給養船隊與河上炮艇；塞米諾爾人一方是自鑄或以皮貨交易得來的燧發滑膛槍，數量有限，火藥與彈藥極度缺乏，不少武器要靠繳獲補充。
kitsEn: The place of the pike in this war is that of a weapon already retired but still leaving a residue of warmth. The pike on the card, dated to 1600, stands for the Spanish tercio of the great square: the pikemen in front met the shock and the shot with a hedge of shafts, while the musketeers behind fired in volleys in the intervals of reloading and fell back behind the pikes to load again. The formation's pike is what let the musketeers stand behind. Thirty years later the pike and shot had been replaced across Europe by the bayonet and the flintlock, and on the Florida frontier of 1817 the American line infantry carried the 1812 and 1814 pattern flintlock smoothbores with bayonets; there were no ranks of pikes left on any battlefield. Yet retirement is not disappearance. First, the Spanish colonial armories in the Florida forts still held pikes and old-style spears left over from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries; when St. Marks and Pensacola changed hands in 1818 that stock passed to the Americans, though it had long been out of any order of battle, and the sources give no count of it, so only the fact itself can be confirmed. Second, the long-hafted points actually in use belonged to the Seminole and Creek warriors and to the Creek and Cherokee auxiliaries in American service, who carried lances, javelins and bows for close assault and pursuit, working together with their muskets: that is what the line on the card means, that after the Mississippi the pike and the musket stood together, one weapon in two periods and two uses. Third, the logic of the pike square was overthrown by artillery in the sieges of 1818: the palisade and the earthwork of Negro Fort took the place of the hedge of pikes, the defenders covered the mouth of the Apalachicola with nine pieces, and the attackers hammered them from several hundred yards with six-pounder guns and twelve-pounder howitzers; the shot that destroyed Negro Fort in 1816 was a heated ball sent into the powder magazine. As for the rest of the equipment, the Americans had line muskets with bayonets, six-pounder guns and twelve-pounder howitzers, carbines and sabres for the cavalry, and a rear service of mules, wagons, supply boats and river gunboats; the Seminoles had flintlock smoothbores of their own casting or bought with hides, few in number, chronically short of powder and cartridges, and many of their weapons were captured American pieces.
tactics: 美軍的戰術底子仍是十九世紀初的線列與齊射：步兵排成密集橫線，齊射後裝填，再以刺刀整齊推進。傑克遜的辦法則是用火與破壞代替會戰——他不去找塞米諾爾人的主力決戰，而是橫掃村社、焚燒房屋與農作物，逼對方餓回沼澤；同時把部隊分成數個縱隊同時推進，一隊沿阿帕拉契科河北岸南下，一隊由弗林特河谷穿越威拉庫奇沼澤直取奧基喬比湖，騎兵與克里克、切羅基輔助部隊在側翼搜索。進入沼澤後橫線拉得很長，砲兵成了唯一能對付密林的手段：斯科特在湖區先用六磅砲直射林緣，把藏在矮樹叢裡的射手逼出來，步兵才得以推進到樹線，鬆軟的沼澤也逼美軍靠船與人力輸送。塞米諾爾人拒絕會戰：他們不給美軍成列的機會，把村社建在沼澤與密林之間，以精準的散射拖住縱隊，用獨木舟沿水道轉移，夜間退回林中，以烽火與信使在村社之間傳遞消息；一八一七年十一月三十日伏擊斯科特中尉的補給船、一八一八年四月十二日在埃康菲納河攻擊麥昆的紅棍聚落，都是這種不求陣地、只求傷敵的作法。守方亦有工事：黑堡的木柵、射擊孔與九門砲構成要塞，而當火藥庫被一發灼熱彈引爆之後，整座木寨連同其中的人一起化為灰燼，也直接催生了傑克遜日後以砲火與火攻對付村社的作風。
tacticsEn: The American tactical foundation remained the line and the volley of the early nineteenth century: infantry in a dense front, fire by ranks, then reload and advance with the bayonet in a disciplined rush. Jackson's method, however, was to substitute fire and destruction for a set-piece battle; instead of seeking out the main body of the Seminoles he swept the villages, burned the houses and the crops, and forced the enemy back into the swamps for want of food, and at the same time he split his force into columns moving at once, one down the north bank of the Apalachicola, another through the Withlacoochee swamp from the Flint valley towards Lake Okeechobee, with cavalry and Creek and Cherokee auxiliaries searching the flanks. Once in the swamps the line had to be stretched to its limit, and artillery was the only answer to the hammock: at the lake Scott first fired his six-pounders straight into the edge of the brush to drive the concealed marksmen out, and only then could the foot advance to the treeline, while the soft ground forced the Americans to move by boat and by manpower. The Seminoles refused a set-piece battle. They never gave the Americans a chance to form line: they sited their villages between swamp and forest, held the columns with accurate scattered shots, moved by dugout canoe along the water lines, retired into the woods at night and passed news from village to village by signal fires and runners. The ambush of Lieutenant Scott's supply boat on 30 November 1817 and the attack on McQueen's Red Stick settlement at the Econfina on 12 April 1818 were both of that kind, seeking no ground but only the enemy's men. The defence had works of its own: the palisade, the embrasures and the nine guns of Negro Fort made a fort, and when a heated ball was sent into the powder magazine the whole wooden works and the men in it were blown away, an episode that directly shaped the artillery-and-fire method Jackson afterwards used against the villages.
data: 數字方面，各家口徑不一，只能取其量級。傑克遜的主力在越境之前於斯科特堡集結，所列的編成為八百名正規步兵、一千名田納西志願兵、一千名喬治亞民兵與約一千四百名下克里克戰士，合計逾四千。一八一七年十一月二十一日與二十二日，蓋恩斯部二百五十人的分隊攻打福爾敦，第二次進攻才把密卡蘇基人逐出村社；同年十一月三十日，斯科特中尉的補給船在阿帕拉契科河上被伏擊，艇上官兵多人遇害，此事成為華盛頓轉向的導火線。一八一八年三月十五日主力越境後，密卡蘇基與塔拉哈西一帶三百餘座房舍被毀。戰役最慘烈的一場是二月十九至二十日的奧基喬比湖之役：斯科特部約一千至一千二百人，配屬數門六磅砲，美軍陣亡約三十人、受傷約一百四十人，美方戰報稱塞米諾爾方面陣亡僅五至七人。四月十二日埃康菲納河之役中，麥昆所率紅棍戰死約四十人。五月二十三日傑克遜率約一千人抵達彭薩科拉時，城內西班牙守軍一百七十五人退入巴蘭卡斯堡，砲戰數日後於五月二十八日投降。一八一六年七月摧毀黑堡的那一發灼熱彈，爆聲在百英里外的彭薩科拉仍可聽聞，堡內堡外自此再無成建制的抵抗。作戰時間自一八一七年十二月到一八一八年九月，主力縱隊自斯科特堡到奧基喬比湖的行軍約一百英里。至一八二三年九月莫爾特里溪會議，約四百二十五名塞米諾爾人出席，換來的保留地約四百萬英畝，範圍自今奧卡拉以北直至坦帕灣南緣。
dataEn: For figures the sources differ in their counting, so only the order of magnitude can be used. Jackson's main force assembled at Fort Scott before crossing the border, and the strength given is eight hundred regular infantry, a thousand Tennessee volunteers, a thousand Georgia militia and about fourteen hundred Lower Creek warriors, more than four thousand in all. On 21 and 22 November 1817 a detachment of two hundred and fifty men under Gaines attacked Fowltown and only the second attempt drove the Mikasukis out of the village; on 30 November of the same year Lieutenant Scott's supply boat was ambushed on the Apalachicola and several of the soldiers aboard were killed, and that was the affair that turned Washington. After the main body crossed on 15 March 1818, more than three hundred houses in the Mikasuki and Tallahassee area were destroyed. The bloodiest engagement was the one at Lake Okeechobee on 19 and 20 February: Scott commanded roughly a thousand to twelve hundred men with several six-pounders, the Americans lost about thirty killed and a hundred and forty wounded, and the American report claimed only five to seven Seminoles killed. In the battle of the Econfina on 12 April about forty Red Sticks under McQueen were killed. On 23 May Jackson reached Pensacola with about a thousand men and found the Spanish garrison of one hundred and seventy-five men withdrawn into Fort Barrancas, which surrendered on 28 May after several days of cannon fire. The heated ball that destroyed Negro Fort in July 1816 was heard in Pensacola a hundred miles away, and organised resistance there ended for good. Active operations ran from December 1817 to September 1818, and the column march from Fort Scott to Lake Okeechobee covered about a hundred miles. At the council of Moultrie Creek in September 1823 about four hundred and twenty-five Seminoles attended and obtained a reservation of about four million acres running from just north of present-day Ocala to a line level with the southern end of Tampa Bay.
cause: 起因有三層。第一層是克里克戰爭留下的廢墟：一八一四年霍斯彎之役與《沃土堡條約》之後，大批克里克人南遷佛羅里達，與塞米諾爾人及黑堡的黑人社群混居，這批人成了美國口中的「逃亡者」，而佛州的存在本身就被南方各州視為奴隸逃亡的漏洞與叛亂的策源地。第二層是邊境暴力：一八一七年蓋恩斯部攻打福爾敦、十一月三十日補給船在阿帕拉契科河被伏擊之後，美國把追捕逃奴與懲罰邊境襲擊合併為一件事，華盛頓改令傑克遜越境追擊，同時默許他攻擊西班牙的要塞。第三層是西班牙的虛弱與固執：一八一七年彭薩科拉守軍司令阿里斯蒂德斯病逝，接任者拒絕交出黑堡的逃亡者，而佛州守軍不足兩百人，談判拖了數年不成。深一層的算盤是地價與棉花：佛羅里達的割讓本就是美國南方擴張的目標，傑克遜本人日後亦被指在彭薩科拉的土地投機中謀利。值得注意的是，越境行動從頭到尾缺乏明確的行政授權，傑克遜事後聲稱有總統密信，實為不實之辭；這場戰爭在很大程度上是邊疆軍人自行擴權的產物，也是美國第一次以追捕逃奴為名、以改變國界為實的軍事行動。
causeEn: The causes lay on three levels. The first was the ruin left by the Creek War: after Horseshoe Bend in 1814 and the Treaty of Fort Jackson, large numbers of Creeks moved south into Florida and mixed with the Seminoles and with the black community of Negro Fort, and these people became the runaways in American accounts, while Florida itself was treated by the southern states as a hole through which slaves escaped and a seedbed of insurrection. The second was the violence of the border: after Gaines's force struck Fowltown in 1817 and a supply boat was ambushed on the Apalachicola on 30 November, the United States merged the recovery of fugitive property with the punishment of border raids, Washington ordered Jackson across the border in pursuit, and at the same time acquiesced in his attack on the Spanish forts. The third was the weakness and the obstinacy of Spain: the commandant of Pensacola, Aristides, died in 1817 and his successor refused to hand over the fugitives of Negro Fort, and with fewer than two hundred men in the province the negotiation dragged on for years without result. A deeper calculation concerned land and cotton: the cession of Florida was an object of southern expansion in its own right, and Jackson himself was later accused of profiting from land speculation at Pensacola. It should be noted that the crossing was never covered by a clear authorisation from Washington; Jackson afterwards claimed a secret message from the President, which was a fabrication. This war was in large part the product of a frontier army officer enlarging his own authority, and it was the first American action fought in the name of recovering fugitives but aimed in fact at a change of frontier.
impact: 影響分國內與國際兩面。在國際上，佛羅里達最終易主：一八一八年五月美國攻佔彭薩科拉，翌年《亞當斯—奧尼斯條約》把東佛羅里達割讓給美國，西佛羅里達由西班牙放棄主權主張，一八二一年完成正式移交，邊界畫在薩賓河，美方同時放棄對德克薩斯的索取。英國為阿布思諾特與阿姆布里斯特兩名英籍人士被處決一事提出交涉，但鑒於美英貿易的比重與英國在北美實力有限，終究沒有報復，兩國反而加緊了合作條約的洽談。西班牙付出了一大塊殖民地，卻也因此擺脫了佛州這個怎麼也守不住的負擔。在國內，這場戰爭留下三筆帳：一是《一八一八年追捕逃亡者法》授權總統在全國任何州動用軍力追捕逃跑的奴隸，為越境用兵開了法律口子；二是國會在同年十二月提出譴責傑克遜越權的決議，雖因他民望太盛未獲通過，「騎在馬背上的人」的疑慮卻一直留到他的總統競選，並衍生出日後所謂「里亞信」的偽造風波；三是對塞米諾爾人而言，佛州北部不再是可居之鄉，一八二三年《莫爾特里溪條約》把保留地劃在半島中部，此後的強制遷徙一路通向一八三五年的第二次塞米諾爾戰爭。軍事上，這場戰爭也示範了另一種版本的有限戰爭：不宣而戰，越境作戰，以追捕逃奴為名而實為改變版圖，而它的成敗與否，最後並不取決於任何一場會戰。
impactEn: The consequences ran along both international and domestic lines. Internationally, Florida changed hands: the Americans took Pensacola in May 1818, the following year the Adams-Onís Treaty ceded East Florida to the United States while Spain renounced all claim to West Florida, and the formal handover was completed in 1821, the boundary being drawn on the Sabine River with the United States dropping its claim to Texas. Britain protested the execution of two British subjects, Arbuthnot and Ambrister, but weighing the weight of Anglo-American trade and its own limited strength in North America it did not retaliate, and the two countries instead tightened the convention they were then negotiating. Spain lost a colony but was also rid of a province it could never hold. At home the war left three bills: the statute of 1818 for the recovery of persons escaping from service authorised the President to use the armed forces in any state of the union and so opened the legal door for troops to cross a frontier; the resolutions introduced in Congress in December 1818 to condemn Jackson's overreach failed because he was too popular, but the fear of a man on horseback stayed with him through his presidential campaigns and produced the later fabrication known as the Rhea letter; and for the Seminoles, northern Florida ceased to be a homeland, the Treaty of Moultrie Creek of 1823 fixing a reservation in the middle of the peninsula, with the forced removals that followed leading straight to the Second Seminole War of 1835. In military terms the war also demonstrated another version of the limited war, fought without a declaration, across a frontier, in the name of recovering fugitives and in fact to move a border, and its outcome was to be decided by no single battle.
result: 結果是美軍在軍事上得手，在政治上卻沒有換來安寧。一八一八年三月以後，密卡蘇基、塔拉哈西與紅棍的主要村社被焚，彼得·麥昆陣亡，鮑萊茲村與黑堡一帶的黑人武裝被拆散，四月佔領聖馬克斯、五月二十八日迫使巴蘭卡斯堡投降之後，佛州全境實際落入美軍控制；九月傑克遜回到斯科特堡宣布戰事結束，命令塞米諾爾人返回原居地，聲明回去者既往不咎。但命令的效果參差：塞米諾爾人沒有接受這場戰爭的結局，大首領帶著人馬退入大沼澤地與大柏樹沼澤，以游擊和狩獵支撐下去，美方記錄中的抵抗一直延續到一八一九年。真正收束這場戰爭的，是一八一九年的割讓條約與一八二三年的《莫爾特里溪條約》：後者以保留地換取塞米諾爾人放棄佛州土地的主權，但各部落的接受程度有限，四百二十五名出席者中真正肯放下抵抗遷徙的只是少數，數百人留在原地拒絕遷移，把衝突推向一八三五年。整場戰爭沒有出現一次可供展示的決定性會戰，美軍的傷亡以數十人陣亡、一百數十人受傷的量級累積，卻換來了佛州，也換來了土地爭端上無法化解的長期對立，並把「用軍隊解決國內的奴隸制度與邊疆問題」這套做法寫進了美國的戰爭史。
resultEn: The result was a military success for the Americans and no peace at all. After March 1818 the main Mikasuki, Tallahassee and Red Stick villages were burned, Peter McQueen was killed, the armed communities of Bowlegs Town and Negro Fort were broken up, and after the seizure of St. Marks in April and the surrender of Fort Barrancas on 28 May the whole of Florida was effectively under American control. In September Jackson returned to Fort Scott, declared the war over and ordered the Seminoles back to their old lands, promising that those who returned would not be molested. The effect of the order was uneven: the Seminoles did not accept the outcome of the war, the great war chiefs took their people into the Everglades and the Big Cypress and supported themselves by hunting and raids, and resistance recorded on the American side ran on to 1819. What actually closed the war was the cession treaty of 1819 and the Treaty of Moultrie Creek of 1823, which exchanged a reservation for the Seminole surrender of all claim to Florida soil; acceptance among the villages was limited, and of the four hundred and twenty-five who attended only a minority were willing to give up resistance and move, while several hundred stayed behind and refused, pushing the conflict towards 1835. No decisive engagement was ever fought. The American losses accumulated in the order of a few score killed and a hundred and more wounded, and what they bought was Florida, an enduring quarrel over land that was never settled, and the addition of a new chapter to American military history: the use of the army to settle the questions of slavery and the frontier at home.
